messages:
incident-bot: [P1] Alert: inference-pool-usw (usw-west-2) reporting 6 nodes NotReady; 18% of pool capacity degraded. Multiple 5xx/timeout spikes in last 3m. PagerDuty triggered.
Erin (SRE): acked. I'm jumping on it — checking node health + kubelet logs.
Erin (SRE): quick check: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=inference-usw -o wide` shows several nodes in NotReady state and a few restarting kubelet.
Erin (SRE): paste: ```
NAME                STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
infer-node-45       NotReady   <none>   34d   v1.24.6
infer-node-46       Ready      <none>   29d   v1.24.6
infer-node-47       NotReady   <none>   12d   v1.24.6
```
Jake (MLOps): on my way, paging in 30s. any immediate customer impact metrics?
Erin (SRE): yes — grafana: inference-5xx-rate spiked to 6% (baseline 0.2%), p95 latency doubled. Affected models: gptx-1 and embed-2048.
Lee (Infra): I'm seeing kubelet crashloops on the NotReady nodes. dmesg on infer-node-45 shows repeated GPU driver resets: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79` and then `kubelet: killing containerd` followed by `kubelet restarted`.
Erin (SRE): could be a driver/GPU OOM cascade — we saw similar pattern with CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT in the past. grabbing kubelet logs: ```
Mar 05 14:02:11 infer-node-45 kubelet[1234]: E0310 14:02:11 kubelet.go:234] container xyz: exit code 137
Mar 05 14:02:12 infer-node-45 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL
Mar 05 14:02:13 infer-node-45 kernel: NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00: GPU is hung
```
oncall-rotation: @Erin want a handoff or do you want to keep on call?
Erin (SRE): Jake take primary please. I'll stay as backup. Jake, see infra notes — likely node-level GPU driver hangs causing kubelet restarts which then flaps pods and triggers eviction cascade.
Jake (MLOps): taking primary. I'm going to cordon+drain the two NotReady nodes to get traffic off them and trigger replacement. command: `kubectl cordon infer-node-45 && kubectl drain infer-node-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
Erin (SRE): note: draining may make pod restarts hit remaining nodes — consider scaling replacement pool before drain.
Lee (Infra): spinning up 4 new nodes in the pool now (aws autoscaling group override). ETA ~3m. I'll also pin the gpu-driver to previous known-good on the new nodes until we investigate the kernel logs.
Customer Success - Maya: CS alert — a handful of customers on us-west reported timeouts and 500s; raising support tickets, some seeing retries/timeouts in production. We need ETA and mitigation ASAP so we can update customers. :worried: 
Jake (MLOps): understood. mitigation plan: 1) cordon NotReady nodes (done), 2) scale + replace nodes (Lee), 3) enable model-fallback to smaller quantized variant for heavy routes to reduce OOM pressure, 4) temporarily route lower-tier traffic to dedicated fallback region. Implementing step 3 now via routing policy.
Erin (SRE): routing change: `rbac-route set routing.infer -> region: fallback-usw, percent: 25 for tier: free` executed by ops-bot.
pagerduty-bot: Incident #INC-2025 created, pager: Jake (MLOps) primary, Erin (SRE) secondary. Severity P1.
Lee (Infra): new nodes have joined: infer-node-51..54 Ready. Not joining GPU driver yet (we're holding on the version).
Jake (MLOps): verifying pod distribution — controllers rescheduled replicas to new nodes, observed reduced eviction events. CPU/GPU utilization on new nodes normal.
Erin (SRE): monitoring: 5xx rate dropping from 6% -> 0.7% over 6m, p95 latency trending down. Customer-facing impact decreasing.
Customer Success - Maya: I'll update customers with: "We observed a node-level GPU/driver issue in us-west causing intermittent failures; mitigation is in progress and service is recovering. We'll follow up with timeline and root cause."
Jake (MLOps): note — one pod had `CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT` before eviction; container logs: ```
E runtime: cuda: launch timeout, killing container
OOM killer invoked: process python3(1234)
```
Erin (SRE): next immediate steps: 1) keep new nodes at previous driver version, 2) collect full dmesg and nvml logs from NotReady nodes before reprovisioning, 3) run targeted regression tests on driver+kernel combo in staging, 4) postmortem.
Lee (Infra): I'll snapshot infer-node-45/47 disks and collect NVML traces. Will isolate nodes from autoscaling pool.
oncall-rotation: handoff: Jake now primary, Erin secondary. Thanks Erin.
Jake (MLOps): confirmed handoff. I'm staying on incident and will kick off postmortem template after stable. Anyone seeing residual 5xx?
Erin (SRE): small tail — 5xx around 0.1% now which is within noisy baseline. Keep monitoring for 30m.
Customer Success - Maya: thanks team. I'll hold customer comms open for any ETA changes.
Jake (MLOps): incident is currently mitigated (traffic normalized, replacement nodes healthy). Creating follow-up ticket INC-2025-RCA and assigning to infra/mlo/serving teams. Action items: collect driver/kernel traces, set automated detector for NVRM Xid 79, run load test on new driver in staging.
Erin (SRE): adding to postmortem: impact window 14:01—14:18 UTC, affected ~12% capacity with customer-facing errors. Will schedule RCA meeting tomorrow. :calendar: 
incident-bot: Incident status updated -> mitigated. Documentation: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2025 (auto-created).
Jake (MLOps): thanks all. If anything flares I'll re-open thread. For now, closing active pager. :thumbsup:
